sections.eyebrow: THE CASE FOR A WHARTON MBA
sections.heading: Powerful tools. Practiced judgment.
sections.quote: In order to get value out of the program, rigor is a necessary condition.
sections.role: Vice Dean of the MBA Program
sections.approvalNote: From Michael Roberts’ interview on the value of a rigorous MBA education.

sections.heading: The future needs more than AI proficiency.
sections.text: Michael Roberts explains why business expertise, AI capability, and sound judgment belong together.

sections.heading: Research. Industry. Classroom. Repeat.
sections.text: Academic research and engagement with industry inform Wharton’s teaching. Questions from executives, alumni, and students help shape what faculty investigate and teach next. Roberts describes a continuous exchange that brings new insights into the classroom as business changes.

stages.label: Research
stages.description: Discover what AI makes possible and where its limits matter.

stages.label: Practice
stages.description: Faculty engage with organizations and executives confronting change.

stages.label: Classroom
stages.description: Turn emerging insight into rigorous, applied learning.

sections.heading: The skills that separate good answers from consequential decisions.

items.title: Think beyond the output
items.description: Interrogate assumptions, evaluate evidence, and determine what an AI-generated answer gets right and what it misses.

items.title: Build solutions
items.description: Combine business expertise and AI capability to build practical solutions—and rethink entire workflows with AI in mind.

items.title: Own the decision
items.description: Explain the analysis, communicate the decision, and take responsibility for the result.

sections.heading: Rigor is how your advantage gets built.
sections.text: Roberts describes an education guided by application and problem-solving. Discussion, communication, and group work help students put ideas into practice. Rigor means doing the thinking and exercising judgment—even when AI can produce an answer.

sections.eyebrow: SCALE WITH THE INSTINCT TO MOVE
sections.heading: A large institution. An entrepreneurial mindset.
sections.text: Wharton’s scale brings faculty expertise across disciplines and alumni experience across industries. Its entrepreneurial spirit helps turn emerging needs into action. Roberts describes school-funded Codex and Claude Code access for MBA students moving from idea to implementation in about a month.

sections.eyebrow: THE PROOF IS IN THE EXPERIENCE
sections.heading: AI isn't a distant subject. It's part of the MBA experience.

items.title: Tools for doing the work
items.description: AI learning begins during Pre-Term. Wharton also provides MBA students with access to ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, and Claude Code. Students must follow each instructor’s expectations for AI use.

items.title: Faculty-led AI workshops
items.description: In fall 2026, Roberts organized a four-part practical AI workshop series with Ethan Mollick, Kartik Hosanagar, and Daniel Rock, sharing how they use AI in their professional and personal lives.

items.title: A dedicated AI MBA major
items.description: The Artificial Intelligence for Business major combines technical fluency with the business, economic, legal, ethical, psychological, and societal dimensions of AI.

sections.heading: From learning AI to building something new.
sections.text: Wharton profiled Hetvee Marviya, WG’27, building an AI-powered platform that turns current events into personalized comic strips for children. In the Generative AI Studio, students develop their ideas through prototyping, critique, and weekly iteration.

sections.heading: The value isn't measured only at graduation.
sections.text: Roberts describes the value of the MBA in both financial and personal terms, including the connections and friendships that can last a lifetime. The case for investing in your education includes the skills you build, the problems you learn to solve, and the people you learn alongside.

action.label: Explore the value of a Wharton MBA

sections.heading: More than a network. People who make time.
sections.text: When Roberts needed help with a research question, a Wharton alum he had never met made time for a conversation that lasted two hours. Another helped him access company data and expertise. For Roberts, that willingness to share time and knowledge without expecting anything in return is what makes Wharton a community.
